label: Planning indication only
note: Every value is editable. 'source' says where it comes from; 'assumption' means no public source was found. Ranges, never a quote.

residential.source: World Bank (Aug 2025), The Syrian Conflict: Physical Damage and Reconstruction Assessment (2011-2024), Annex, Table 8 and text: housing reconstruction at 2.1x the baseline unit cost is roughly US$600/m2, including rubble clearance, site inspection and removal of unexploded ordnance. https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102025095540101/pdf/P510947-f30bd5f6-78d5-4712-9f1e-a558b5c8ba75.pdf
residential.adjustment: Different country: range set at -25% to +50% of US$600/m2 because Lebanese building costs are likely higher. To check against the housing chapter of the World Bank Lebanon RDNA (March 2025).

non_residential.source: Same World Bank Syria assessment (Aug 2025): public or commercial buildings at 2.3x the baseline unit cost, about US$800/m2.
non_residential.adjustment: Range -25% to +50% of US$800/m2, as for housing.

damage_share.source: doc 24 section 9 (reuses the displacement shares: destroyed and severe 100%, moderate 50%, possible 20%)

crews.source: No public source found for contractor crews in south Lebanon. Two scales: one H3 r8 neighbourhood, and the whole demo box. Edit to the planned number of crews.

m2_per_crew_month.source: No public source found. Floor area one crew rebuilds per month; edit with contractor figures.

start_delay_months.source: No public source found. Covers assessment, rubble clearance and unexploded-ordnance clearance before building (the World Bank Syria assessment names these steps but gives no durations).

context.lebanon_total_needs: World Bank Lebanon RDNA (7 March 2025): recovery and reconstruction needs about US$11 billion for 8 Oct 2023 to 20 Dec 2024, housing the largest share. https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2025/03/07/lebanon-s-recovery-and-reconstruction-needs-estimated-at-us-11-billion
